prs.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP POST errors
prs.author: pragnyanramtha
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When a streamable HTTP request encounters an error (connection death, server crash, or HTTP 4xx/5xx), the client hangs forever instead of receiving a proper JSONRPCError response. All three PRs fix this by catching errors in `_handle_post_request` / `handle_request_async` and writing a `JSONRPCError` back to `read_stream_writer` rather than letting the caller block indefinitely. (3 PRs)

PR #1578 adds a similar `_send_error_response` helper but only at the transport-error layer and has no test changes visible in the diff. clusters.pick_reason: PR #2410 widens the `errlog` type signature to `TextIO | int`, giving callers explicit control (e.g., pass `subprocess.DEVNULL` to silence stderr in Jupyter). This is a clean, testable, general-purpose fix that covers Jupyter and any other environment where a raw file descriptor is preferable. PR #2020's approach — runtime Jupyter detection via IPython internals — is environment-specific, harder to unit-test, and fragile against changes to IPython's class hierarchy. The #2410 solution subsumes the Jupyter use case without tying behavior to environment sniffing.
